note: Recorded 15 Nov from the fal backend (OpenRouter) for the select call on a yoga e2e run: every score has changes 0.
idea: A booking page for a small yoga studio.

candidates.decision: Who the page serves first: regulars or newcomers
options: Regulars who book weekly
First-time visitors
Both equally
candidates.recommendation: Regulars who book weekly
candidates.reason: A small studio lives on repeat attendance, and her journey already has a 'Book your usual' shortcut for them.
candidates.question: What makes someone come back to a studio week after week?

candidates.decision: How 'Book your usual' works from the classes list
options: One tap rebooks their last class next week
Shows their usual class to confirm first
Leave it out until evidence exists
candidates.recommendation: Shows their usual class to confirm first
candidates.reason: It keeps the shortcut fast but still passes through confirm, so people never book the wrong class by accident.
candidates.question: How much should the page remember about someone before they've said anything?

candidates.decision: What happens when a class is full
options: Show as full, no other option
Offer a waitlist
Show as full and suggest the next similar class
candidates.recommendation: Show as full and suggest the next similar class
candidates.reason: It keeps the smallest end-to-end version while not leaving the customer at a dead end.

candidates.decision: What confirm asks for and what it promises about cancelling
options: Name and email only, with a plain cancel-by time
Account sign-up plus payment
Name and email, no stated cancel policy
candidates.recommendation: Name and email only, with a plain cancel-by time
candidates.reason: Minimal fields keep booking quick, and a clear cancel-by line sets expectations before the customer commits.

candidates.decision: The one number that says the booking page worked
options: Share of visitors who reach booked
Count of bookings per week
Share of booked people who attend
candidates.recommendation: Share of visitors who reach booked
candidates.reason: A visit-to-booked rate shows whether the whole journey works, whatever the traffic.
candidates.question: What would tell you, a month in, that the page is truly working for your studio?

candidates.decision: What we measure at Book your usual
options: Count of Book your usual taps that end in booked
Count of returning customers who book at all
Don't measure it yet
candidates.recommendation: Count of Book your usual taps that end in booked
candidates.reason: It shows whether the shortcut for regulars finishes bookings, which decides if it stays.
candidates.question: What makes someone come back to a studio week after week?

candidates.decision: What we measure at confirm
options: Share of confirm views that become booked
Time spent on confirm
Count of confirm errors
candidates.recommendation: Share of confirm views that become booked
candidates.reason: Drop-off at the last step before booking is where lost bookings show up most clearly.

candidates.decision: What we keep from each booking at booked
options: Name, email, class, time; deleted after 12 months
Email and class only; deleted after 3 months
Full profile kept until the customer asks to delete
candidates.recommendation: Name, email, class, time; deleted after 12 months
candidates.reason: It holds only what we need to send reminders and count repeat visits, and it sets a clear end date for personal data.

candidates.decision: Who the page is built for first: regulars or newcomers
options: Regulars who book weekly
First-time visitors
Both equally
candidates.recommendation: Regulars who book weekly
candidates.reason: A small studio's steady income comes from people who return, and the 'Book your usual' path already points that way, but we'd want to check this with the studio's own booking history first.
candidates.question: What makes someone come back to a studio week after week?

candidates.decision: What the main problem is that the page solves
options: Finding a class that fits my schedule
Booking quickly with little effort
Feeling sure my spot is held
candidates.recommendation: Booking quickly with little effort
candidates.reason: We have no evidence yet, so the first thing to learn is what currently makes booking hard, by asking a few students and the owner how they book today.
candidates.question: What gets in the way when someone tries to book a class today?

candidates.decision: Whether a first-time visitor must create an account before booking
options: No account, just name and email
Account required
Optional account after booking
candidates.recommendation: No account, just name and email
candidates.reason: The smallest end-to-end version asks for the least, and we'd learn from drop-off whether people want accounts at all.

candidates.decision: How payment or class passes fit into the confirm step
options: Pay at the studio, book only online
Pay online per class
Use existing class pass or pay online
candidates.recommendation: Pay at the studio, book only online
candidates.reason: Taking money is a promise that can't be cleanly undone, so we'd first learn how students pay now before building it.
candidates.question: How do students pay for classes at this studio today?

candidates.decision: Whether a returning visitor gets a one-tap 'Book your usual' shortcut
options: On, remembered on this device only
On, tied to an account login
Off for now
candidates.recommendation: On, remembered on this device only
candidates.reason: A device-stored last booking needs no accounts and is the simplest thing that makes the n1 to n5 path work.
candidates.question: What makes someone come back to a studio week after week, and how should the page honour that?

candidates.decision: What happens when two people take the last spot
options: First confirmed booking wins, the other sees 'just filled' and nearby classes
Hold the spot for a few minutes during confirm
Allow overbooking and sort it out by hand
candidates.recommendation: First confirmed booking wins, the other sees 'just filled' and nearby classes
candidates.reason: An atomic check at confirm is the proven way to avoid double booking without holds or timers.

candidates.decision: Whether full classes get a waitlist
options: Waitlist switch on
Waitlist off, show 'full' only
Show 'full' with a link to the next class
candidates.recommendation: Waitlist off, show 'full' only
candidates.reason: The smallest end-to-end version ships without waitlist logic, and it can be switched on later with evidence.

candidates.decision: How the booking is confirmed and what is stored
options: Show confirmation on page plus email, storing name and email only
Page confirmation only, no message sent
Email and text, storing phone as well
candidates.recommendation: Show confirmation on page plus email, storing name and email only
candidates.reason: Email is cheap and reliable, and collecting the least data avoids promises that cannot be undone.

candidates.decision: What booking should feel like: quick and remembered, or guided and reassuring
options: Quick and remembered
Guided and reassuring
Quick for regulars, guided for first-timers
candidates.recommendation: Quick for regulars, guided for first-timers
candidates.reason: One filled button marks the main action, so the first screen leads with either 'Book your usual' or the class list, and the grey wireframes depend on which one it is.
candidates.question: What makes someone come back to a studio week after week?

candidates.decision: What leads the classes screen and how dense the list is
options: Day-by-day list: time, class, teacher, spots left
Cards with photos and class descriptions
Week grid
candidates.recommendation: Day-by-day list: time, class, teacher, spots left
candidates.reason: Hierarchy by size and contrast, not decoration, keeps the list scannable at 390px with 44px tap rows and no sideways scroll.

candidates.decision: What a full class shows and what the customer can do next
options: Greyed row labelled 'Full' with a waitlist button
Hidden from the list
Greyed row labelled 'Full' with next similar class
candidates.recommendation: Greyed row labelled 'Full' with next similar class
candidates.reason: A visible full state with a next step avoids a dead end, and it keeps the smallest version working end to end without waitlist mechanics.

candidates.decision: Where 'Book your usual' sits and how it behaves
options: Top of the classes screen, one tap to the confirm step
Inside the class detail only
Left out of the first version
candidates.recommendation: Top of the classes screen, one tap to the confirm step
candidates.reason: It skips the class step for returning customers, and the confirm screen stays the one place that takes the booking so nothing is booked by accident.
candidates.question: Who is the person you picture booking this page most often?

candidates.decision: Whether booking takes payment online or leaves it for the desk
options: Pay online when booking
Pay at the desk
Online or desk, customer picks
candidates.recommendation: Pay online when booking
candidates.reason: A booking that ends in 'booked' with money settled gives the smallest working end-to-end version and cuts no-shows.
candidates.question: What would make someone feel the class is truly theirs the moment they book it?

candidates.decision: What people buy: single classes, class packs, or a membership
options: Single classes only
Single classes plus a class pack
Single, pack and monthly membership
candidates.recommendation: Single classes plus a class pack
candidates.reason: Drop-ins let newcomers try the studio and a pack rewards regulars without the upkeep of recurring billing, and extras wait for evidence.
candidates.question: Who is the person you picture booking here, and how often do they come?

candidates.decision: Refund and credit rules when someone cancels late or the studio cancels
options: Full refund early, credit if late, full refund if studio cancels
Credit only, never cash back
No refunds, studio decides case by case
candidates.recommendation: Full refund early, credit if late, full refund if studio cancels
candidates.reason: A clear cutoff time protects the teacher's income while being fair when the studio is the one that cancels.
candidates.question: How should it feel to cancel a class you have already paid for?

candidates.decision: Whether first-timers get an intro offer, and what shape it takes
options: No intro offer, one price for all
Discounted first class
Intro pack of a few classes for a set period
candidates.recommendation: Discounted first class
candidates.reason: A low-risk first booking gives new people a reason to book now, and the 'Book your usual' path then serves those who return.
